name: reducer_error
summary: The bytes decoded but the reducer refused them.
trigger: The reducer returned an error for a request/response pair that passed every earlier gate.
grounding: The last policy gate, and contract for the same reason as the rest: two implementations whose reducers disagree about what is reducible capture different sessions. Everything upstream of it said the turn was capturable in principle — right path, right method, readable bytes, a known provider — so a count here means the content itself was not a turn, and that is a distinct thing for an operator to chase.
not_expressible: Expressing it needs provider wire bytes and a reducer to run them through. Those exist as fixtures already — pkg/capture/fixtures/ and fixtures/recordings/ — and belong there rather than duplicated into a vocabulary corpus.
notes: A reducer that SUCCEEDS but produces empty content is not this reason and is not a drop at all: the turn is dispatched and the emptiness is metered separately. Conflating the two would hide a dispatched-but-contentless turn behind a drop counter.
